ios.//: Reverse-DNS of the GitHub org that hosts this, not a domain: `pew2.dev` is not registered, and an identifier built from a domain someone else can buy is a claim that can be contested after the app is on a store — at which point it cannot be changed without shipping a new app. Fork this and you must change it: an identifier is unique per store, and a fork keeping this one cannot be submitted alongside the original.

infoPlist.//: True because pew2 ships its own cryptography: @noble/ciphers implements XChaCha20-Poly1305 for the end-to-end encryption between phone and daemon. The exemption this key asks about covers encryption provided by the operating system — HTTPS through URLSession, Keychain, CryptoKit — and not a bundled crypto engine. This was `false` while the app only spoke TLS, and leaving it there after adding E2EE would be a false declaration on a binding export-control statement, not merely a wrong build setting. App Store Connect will now ask the export-compliance questionnaire; standard published algorithms used this way generally fall under the mass-market exemption, but that determination and the annual self-classification report are yours to make.

plugins.//: Without this the generated splash is pure white while the app's own background is #111111 with userInterfaceStyle dark, so every cold launch flashed white before painting. No `dark` variant: the app is dark-only, and declaring one conflicts with the app-wide userInterfaceStyle. The colour is theme.color.bg, kept in step by hand because app.json cannot import it.

One string for two uses: scanning the pairing code, and taking a photo to send an agent. expo-image-picker writes the same Info.plist key, so its own cameraPermission is deliberately left unset rather than fighting this one.
plugins.cameraPermission: Used to scan the pairing code shown on your computer, and to take photos you send to your agent.

plugins.//: No photosPermission here on purpose: expo-media-library below writes the same NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription key and runs later, so a string here would be overwritten and the attach prompt would explain saving instead of attaching. That one string covers both uses.

plugins.microphonePermission: Used only to dictate a message, while the mic button is on.
plugins.speechRecognitionPermission: Used only to turn what you dictate into the text of a message.

plugins.savePhotosPermission: Used only to save images your agent sends you.
plugins.photosPermission: Used only to attach photos you pick, and to save images your agent sends you.
